lead: Low-rise houses with gardens and streets named after flowers, on the slope of Montjuïc, beside Gran Via.
text: It is a small neighbourhood, of 0.30 km², on the north-west side of Montjuïc, which was born with the vocation of a garden city. Hence its low-rise houses with gardens and its streets with flower names, such as Dàlia, Lotus, Hortènsia, Begònia and Crisantem, which contrast with the tall buildings of Gran Via.

Here you live beside Plaça d'Espanya and the hill, with two works by Josep Puig i Cadafalch as landmarks: the former Casarramona factory, now home to CaixaForum, and the Font del Gat restaurant. With 10,869 inhabitants, it is a neighbourhood on a human scale beside one of the city's great squares.
housing: Low-rise houses with gardens on the slope and tall blocks beside Gran Via.
